name: Rest Assured
subtitle: Because Death Should Rest in Peace — Not in Pieces.

description.low:
Obsidian, and a great deal of it. The stone does not reflect the violet overhead; it takes it in and returns nothing, so that the building reads at distance as a hole in the town cut roughly to the shape of a building. Fractal work is etched across the whole face of it, fine as frost, and it holds still under a direct look and is doing something else at the corner of the eye.

The slogan is over the door in letters of restrained gold: BECAUSE DEATH SHOULD REST IN PEACE — NOT IN PIECES. Inside, the silence is not the absence of noise. It is a maintained condition, the way a temperature is maintained, and it costs something to run.

The vaults go back further than the building goes back. Nobody who works here regards that as a fact about the building.
description.mid: Obsidian that takes the violet in and returns nothing, so the place reads as a hole cut to the shape of a building. Fractal etching, still under a direct look and busy at the edge of the eye. BECAUSE DEATH SHOULD REST IN PEACE — NOT IN PIECES. Inside, the silence is maintained rather than natural, and the vaults go back further than the building does.
description.high: Obsidian, fractal etching, maintained silence. The vaults go back further than the building.

revisit.low: Soliloquy is where she was, at an angle she has not adjusted, and the count of vaults along the near wall is not the count you left with. You have stopped doing the count aloud. She noticed that you stopped, and approved, and said so in a way that took ninety seconds and rhymed twice.
revisit.mid: Soliloquy has not adjusted her angle. The count along the near wall has changed again. You have stopped doing it aloud; she noticed, and approved, at length.
revisit.high: The count along the near wall has changed again.

lucid.2: The whispers in the air here are not consistent in language but are consistent in rhythm, and the rhythm is a sentence being composed rather than a sentence being spoken.
lucid.3: Under the whispering: paper. Not turning — being *fed*, drawn round a roller one line at a time, and then the small definite noise of a lever thrown at the end of it.
lucid.4: There is no whispering. There has never been whispering. There is a room somewhere with a machine in it, and this building is what the sound of that machine looks like when it is given somewhere to be.

ambient: The temperature in the west corridor drops eleven degrees between one vault and the next, and comes back up between the next and the one after, and nothing accounts for either.
Your watch, which is stopped, is stopped at a different time in this room, and is stopped at 3:33 again by the door.
A whisper resolves for one whole second into a complete sentence — '...and he never once asked who was paying for the vault' — and unresolves before you can decide whether it was about you.

objects.name: the vault plates

description.low:
Brass, recessed, one to a door, engraved to a standard that suggests the engraver was paid by the hour and enjoyed the work. Name, two dates, and a line of the family's choosing.

The trick — and it is done to everyone, and Soliloquy will confirm it without being asked and without being helpful — is that on first look the plate carries your own name. Not a resemblance. Your name, your spelling, the middle one included, which is not a name you have used in public since a form in 1994. It holds for less than a second and then it is a stranger's, and the stranger's dates are ordinary, and the family's chosen line is something about a garden.
description.mid: Brass plates, one to a door: name, two dates, a chosen line. On first look each carries your own name — spelling and middle name included, a name you have not used in public since 1994 — for under a second. Then it is a stranger's, with ordinary dates and something about a garden.
description.high: Each brass plate shows your full name for under a second, then a stranger's.

objects.repeat: It happens on every plate and it has not stopped happening. The middle name is the detail you keep returning to. Nobody in Silvora Reefs knows the middle name.

lucid.3: The second date on your name is not blank. You have never got a clean look at it and you have stopped pretending that is bad luck.

objects.monocle: The gold holds your name on the plate instead of letting it go. OLIVER OTTO ONIONS, and beneath it two dates, and the second one is legible and is not far off and is written in the same hand as the three dry pages in your notebook.

passive.text: Everyone gets this. That is the reported effect and Soliloquy confirms it. But everyone getting their own name is a mirror, and a mirror does not know a middle name that has not been spoken aloud in thirty years.

Watch Soliloquy while you read a plate. She does not watch the plate. She watches your face for the half-second the name is yours, and what is on her face is not amusement. It is the expression of somebody checking that a thing is still going wrong the way it is supposed to.

clue.title: Your name on every plate
clue.text: Every vault plate carries your full name — including a middle name unspoken in thirty years — for under a second before resolving to a stranger's.

clue.title: The second date
clue.text: Held under the monocle, your name stays on the plate, and the second date is legible, and it is written in the same hand as the three dry pages.

check.prompt: Nineteen vault plates, struck and mounted. Read all nineteen rather than the one with your name on it.
check.success:
Nineteen names. You know four of them and three of those four are people you have met tonight.

And the strike depth is not uniform: eighteen are stamped to the same depth, and one — the seventh — is shallower, and struck twice, the second strike slightly off the first, as though the name on it had been changed to itself.
check.failure: Nineteen plates, brass, mounted, and one of them with your name on it, and after that the other eighteen are extremely difficult to give any attention to at all.

clue.title: Struck twice, to itself
clue.text: The seventh vault plate at Rest Assured is shallower than the rest and struck twice, the second strike slightly off — a name changed to itself.

objects.name: the unmarked vault

description.low:
Third from the end of the west corridor, and it has no plate. Not a blank plate — no plate, no recess, no screw holes, no discolouration where a plate has been taken off. The door was made without provision for one.

The seam around it is not sealed. It stands very slightly ajar, at a width of perhaps two fingers, and it has stood at exactly that width every time you have been in this corridor. Through it there is light: warm, low, single-source, of the kind a lamp with a green shade makes.

You have never got closer than eight feet. Not because you are prevented. Because on each approach Soliloquy has arrived beside you with something to say, and the something has always been long, and by the end of it you have been somewhere else.
description.mid: Third from the end, west corridor, no plate — no recess, no screw holes, no provision ever made. It stands two fingers ajar, at exactly that width every time, with warm low light behind it of the kind a green-shaded lamp makes. You have never got closer than eight feet; Soliloquy always arrives with something long to say.
description.high: The unmarked vault stands two fingers ajar. Green lamplight behind it. You have never got closer than eight feet.

objects.repeat: Two fingers. Always two fingers. A door that has been left ajar is a door somebody intends to come back through.

lucid.2: The light behind it moves when the whispering pauses.
lucid.4: It is not ajar. It is being *held* ajar, at a width somebody has chosen, so that the light gets out and you do not get in.

objects.monocle: Through the gold, the gap widens to the width of a doorway without the door moving, and behind it is your desk. Not a desk of the same make. Yours: the door on two trestles, the drift of paper, the trestle with the split in the left leg that you have been meaning to see to since before the water. And on it, in the rectangle where your dust says nothing has ever stood, a typewriter, with a page in it, and the page is not blank.

passive.text: Every single time. She arrives at eight feet, not seven, not nine. That is not vigilance. That is a marked position, and somebody marked it.

A door manufactured without provision for a plate was manufactured for a vault that was never going to be assigned an occupant. This one was not overlooked. It was built empty and kept empty and kept ajar.

check.prompt: She will arrive at eight feet with something long to say. She always does. So give her something longer to say first, and walk while she is saying it.
check.success:
You start talking before she does. You start on the slogan — on the em dash in it, on the decision to break REST IN PEACE against NOT IN PIECES on a hyphen that is doing the work of a whole theology, on whether a house that advertises against dismemberment is reassuring the bereaved or the merchandise.

It is not your best. It is your longest, and length is the currency here, and Soliloquy is a woman constitutionally unable to let a speech go unanswered. She answers. She answers at length, in rhyme, with a hand raised to hold her place — and a hand raised to hold a place is a hand not raised to stop you.

Seven feet. Six. At four you can see the split in the left trestle leg.

At three she stops mid-line, and the silence in this building is a maintained condition and she has just switched it off, and the sound underneath it is a machine typing very fast.

'Not that one,' she says, in her own voice, which you have not heard before and which has no rhyme in it at all. 'I have kept that one shut for you, Mr Onions, and I would like it noted that I have never once been thanked.'
check.failure:
You open on the slogan and she takes the em dash off you inside a sentence.

She has been waiting years for somebody to raise the em dash. What follows is nine minutes on punctuation as a mortuary practice, delivered without a breath you can get a foot into, and at some point during it you have been walked — gently, courteously, without a hand laid on you — back down the corridor to the vestibule, where the door is, and where the sound of a machine typing is not audible at all.

clue.title: Your desk, in a vault
clue.text: Behind the unmarked door: your desk. The split in the left trestle leg included. And on it, a typewriter, with a page in it that is not blank.

clue.title: Kept shut, deliberately
clue.text: Soliloquy does not guard the unmarked vault the way she guards the others. She guards it the way somebody guards a thing they have decided you should not have yet.

objects.name: the interment ledger

description.low:
On a stand by the vestibule, open, because Soliloquy holds that the dead have nothing to hide and the living should be encouraged in the habit.

Columns: NAME. RECEIVED. VAULT. PAID BY. It runs back a long way in several hands and one ink.

The PAID BY column is the one. Family, family, estate, family, parish, family — and then, at intervals of no pattern you can find, a run of entries where the column reads only: ACCOUNT SETTLED IN ADVANCE BY THE COALITION. Forty or so, scattered across decades. The names in those rows are not remarkable. The dates in those rows are not remarkable. What they have in common is not in the ledger.
description.mid: NAME. RECEIVED. VAULT. PAID BY. Mostly family and estates — and then, at no pattern, forty-odd rows reading only ACCOUNT SETTLED IN ADVANCE BY THE COALITION. Nothing else connects them.
description.high: Forty-odd interments across the decades read: ACCOUNT SETTLED IN ADVANCE BY THE COALITION.

objects.repeat: You count the Coalition rows again and get a different number again, and this time you were watching your own finger.
objects.monocle: Through the gold the Coalition rows have a further column that the page does not otherwise carry, headed REASON, and every entry in it says the same three words: NOTICED TOO MUCH.

passive.text: Settled in advance. Not settled — settled *in advance*. Somebody paid for these vaults before the people in them needed vaults, which means somebody knew, and the interesting question is not how they knew. It is how far in advance.
Soliloquy leaves this ledger open on a stand in the doorway. She wants it read. She has wanted it read for some time, by somebody who would do more than count.

clue.title: Settled in advance by the Coalition
clue.text: Forty-odd interments across several decades were paid for by the Quad-C before the occupants required them.

clue.title: NOTICED TOO MUCH
clue.text: Under the monocle the prepaid rows carry a column the page does not have. Every entry reads: NOTICED TOO MUCH.

check.prompt: The ledger is open and the hand is copperplate. Go through it against everything you have ever read about how these are kept.
check.success:
Vault ledgers run to a form, and the form has been the same for two hundred years: date of lease, name of lessee, term, and a countersign.

This one has all four columns and the dates in the first column are *later* than the countersigns in the fourth. Every entry was signed off before it was made. For nineteen vaults. In copperplate, without a single correction, which is not how a man writes when he is making it up as he goes.
check.failure: Copperplate, four columns, two hundred years of convention behind it. Something about the ordering is wrong and the wrongness will not resolve into a sentence, and the keeper is watching you not resolve it with enormous courtesy.

clue.title: Countersigned before it was written
clue.text: Every entry in the Rest Assured ledger was countersigned before its own lease date. Nineteen vaults, no corrections.

objects.name: a brass plaque with no name on it

description.low:
Set into the wall of the vestibule at the height of a plate, in the same brass, by the same hand. It carries no name and no dates. It carries a number, five digits, engraved.

Engraved. Not printed, not displayed, not on any mechanism. Cut into brass, permanently, by a tool.

It was 04412 the first time you saw it. It is not 04412 now.
description.mid: A brass plaque at plate height with no name and no dates. Five engraved digits — cut into the metal, not displayed by any mechanism. It was 04412 the first time. It is not now.
description.high: A brass plaque carrying five engraved digits. The number has changed since you last read it.

objects.repeat: Lower. Always lower. Nobody has been near it and there is no tool in this building that could have been.
objects.monocle: The gold shows the brass mid-cut: a burin in the metal, moving, unheld, and behind it the ghosts of every number it has been, stacked back through 04412 and past it, thousands of them, all the way to a first cut that is out of sight below the plaque and going down.

passive.text: A counter has a mechanism. This has a chisel mark. Somebody is re-engraving a brass plaque, by hand, at a rate you have not caught, to keep a count that nobody has posted the purpose of.

Five digits, on a plate, in a mausoleum, unlabelled. The absence of the label is the message: everybody who needs to know what it counts down to already knows, and the plaque is not there to inform them. It is there so they cannot say they were not warned.

clue.title: The engraved countdown
clue.text: A nameless brass plaque in the vestibule carries five hand-engraved digits. The number falls. No mechanism is involved and no purpose is posted.

check.prompt: The countdown is running and it is running toward something. Stand here and watch it without looking away and without deciding in advance what it means.
check.success:
You hold. It runs. It does not speed up because you are watching and it does not stop because you would prefer it to, and after a while the important thing about it becomes clear, which is that it is not a threat.

It is a *deadline*. Somebody set it. Somebody has been working against it. And a deadline is the only kind of clock that can be missed on purpose.
check.failure:
You hold for as long as you hold, and then the arithmetic gets into you — how long, and until what, and what happens to a parish when a clock somebody else set runs out — and you are looking at the wall instead, and the wall is a great deal easier.

When you look back the count is lower and you have no idea by how much.

clue.title: A deadline, not a threat
clue.text: The countdown at Rest Assured is a deadline somebody set and has been working against — the only kind of clock that can be missed on purpose.

objects.name: the whispers

description.low:
They travel in the air rather than along the stone, which is the wrong way round for a building of this shape, and they are constant, and they are almost words.

Stand still and give them a minute and they resolve. Not into a voice — into a *sentence*, assembled out of the general susurrus by the same trick that assembles a face out of wallpaper. They are all on one subject. They are about death, and they are about dreams, and they never mention one without the other, and the grammar of them is careful in a way that overheard speech is not.
description.mid: Constant, almost words, travelling through the air rather than along the stone — which is the wrong way round here. Given a minute they resolve into sentences, always about death and dreams together, and the grammar is more careful than overheard speech has any business being.
description.high: The whispers resolve, given a minute. Always death and dreams together, in careful grammar.

objects.repeat: They have got easier to resolve. This is not the direction that sort of thing usually goes.
objects.monocle: The gold does nothing to them, because they are not visual, and the failure is informative: the monocle reveals what a thing is made of, and it has no opinion about these at all, the way it has no opinion about your own voice.

check.prompt: Stop trying to hear the words. Listen for who is talking.
check.success:
You stop reaching for the words and let the room have them, and what comes up out of the susurrus is not vocabulary. It is cadence.

It is yours. Every whisper in this building is in your cadence — the long clause, the qualifying aside, the pause before the last word that you have never once managed to stop putting there. Forty voices, none of them yours, all of them speaking the way you speak.

They are not the dead. They are not talking about you. They are *drafts* of you, and this is where they have been put.
check.failure: You listen for the speaker and get the words instead, and the words this time are '—should rest in peace, not in—' and then the building's slogan, and then the slogan again, and then a stretch that is only the rhythm of the slogan with different syllables in it, and none of it will hold still long enough to have said anything.

clue.title: Forty voices, one cadence
clue.text: The whispers in Rest Assured are all in your cadence. Not the dead, and not about you: drafts of you, stored.

objects.name: the unmarked vault, standing open
objects.description:
Two fingers has become a doorway. The measurement Soliloquy has taken every Michaelmas for eleven years, the only measurement in Silvora Reefs that never disagreed with itself, has finally disagreed with itself.

She is standing beside it with her hands folded and she is not saying anything, in a building where silence is a maintained condition and she is the one who maintains it.
objects.monocle: The gold shows the desk, the split trestle, the green lamp, the page in the machine — and a second chair, which has not been there before, drawn up at an angle that means somebody expects to be talked to.
objects.repeat: Still open. It is not going to close on its own, and that is not the same as it being patient.

passive.text: Every deduction you have made for a fortnight terminates here. There is nothing further to work out. The next thing is not a conclusion, it is a step.
Four inches of nothing, and a floor on the other side that will take a man's weight. The body has already decided. It has been leaning that way since the harbour.

check.prompt:
Go through. Nothing is stopping you and nothing has been stopping you for some time, and that is the part that will need thinking about afterwards, on the other side, if there is an afterwards and if there is a side.

There is no way back through a seam. Whatever is unfinished in Silvora Reefs stays unfinished.
check.success:
You go through.

There is no membrane and no cold and no drama, and the last thing behind you is somebody not saying anything, and then you are standing on boards in a room nine feet by eleven with a green-shaded lamp in it.
check.failure:
Your foot goes over the edge and your weight does not follow it, and you stand for a while in a doorway with one leg committed, which is not a dignified way to arrive anywhere and is a completely honest description of the last fortnight.

Then the knee that has been going since the harbour makes the decision for you, and you go through badly, and land on boards, in a room nine feet by eleven, with a green-shaded lamp in it.

exits.hang_hi: down out of the obsidian to a floor that hangs from nothing
exits.durry_kwain: down the hill toward vanilla, which after this will be welcome
exits.mobius: along and down to the red frontage and the light that is nearly red
exits.giddyup: along the ridge to smoke, and a table with names under it
